meta_title: Security and Privacy: Exact Permissions, Nothing More
meta_description: Baton's security architecture: explicitly scoped GitHub permissions, signed webhooks with HMAC-SHA256, session encryption, and strict data isolation.
h1: Exact permissions. No stored source code.
intro: Baton is engineered so that even in the absolute worst-case scenario, the app holds no permissions to read your source code, inspect repository files, or access production secrets.
principle_webhook_body: Every incoming GitHub webhook delivery is authenticated against your configured webhook secret using HMAC-SHA256 with the x-hub-signature-256 header. Signatures are evaluated in constant time to prevent timing side-channel attacks before any JSON payload is parsed.
principle_retention_body: We store only operational metadata required to render the dashboard and measure stall durations: PR titles, numbers, author logins, and timestamps. On uninstall, all PR snapshots and repository configurations are deleted immediately and permanently.
principle_tenant_body: Every dashboard query is strictly scoped to the authenticated GitHub OAuth user and installations they own or belong to. Sessions are backed by 32 cryptographically random bytes, hashed with SHA-256 before storage, and protected by httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies.
principle_disclosure_body: If you identify a security vulnerability in Baton, notify us immediately at security@baton.dev. We acknowledge reports within 24 hours and commit to transparent patching and public attribution.
cta_title: Need a custom security review or SOC2 report?
cta_body: Our Organization plan includes vendor assessment assistance, SAML SSO, and audit log exports.
row_1_purpose: Read PR review states and update the single pinned status comment and nudges.
row_2_purpose: Synchronize canonical baton:* state labels on GitHub pull requests.
row_3_purpose: Inspect check-suite pass/fail conclusions to avoid nudging reviewers on red builds.
row_4_purpose: Read repository names, owner logins, and default branch references.
row_5_purpose: Baton never requests or touches file contents, source code, or git blobs.
row_6_purpose: Cannot view workflow secrets, CI definitions, or runner configurations.
row_7_purpose: Cannot modify repo settings, invite members, or manage organization keys.
